title: Cooperative stream timeout handoff adapter and practical examples for Go SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Go consumers of the Redwood streaming API continue to encounter surprising cancellation races when client deadlines, network retries, and server-initiated disconnects interact. Current examples in docs show naive context cancellation usage which leads to resource leaks or dropped traceability in production. Goal: implement a small, reusable adapter in the Go SDK that provides a cooperative timeout-handoff pattern, plus a cookbook of idiomatic examples and migration notes for existing integrations.

Scope: a) library-level adapter that exposes a StreamWithHandoff(ctx, streamFn, opts) helper which coordinates an outer request context and internal per-message soft deadlines; b) ergonomic iterator helpers for resumable reads that preserve partial results when the application extends deadlines; c) clear guidance and examples for the common patterns: cancel-to-abort, cancel-to-soft-extend, and graceful client disconnect.

Non-goals: changing server protocol or introducing new wire-level framing. Avoid adding global goroutine managers; keep the adapter composable and opt-in.

Why now: multiple production incidents and customer support tickets show apps retrying entire prompts after transient client timeouts, inflating token cost. A small SDK improvement can reduce these retries and make graceful shutdown behavior predictable.
acceptance_criteria: Add StreamHandoff adapter implemented in Go SDK with comprehensive unit tests
Provide three runnable examples in docs: (1) immediate cancel/abort, (2) soft-extend per-message deadline, (3) resumable iterator that returns last-acknowledged position
Benchmarks demonstrate that using the adapter reduces unnecessary full-request retries in our internal simulation by >=40% for common timeout distributions
Migration guide and API docs added in SDK repo and Console quickstart
Code review landed and a follow-up PR for docs integration is opened
implementation_notes: Design decision: use explicit per-message softDeadline context created from parent ctx with CancelFunc that only influences prefetch/read loops, not final commit/ack path
Adapter exposes hooks for onExtend(ctx, tokenPos) and onAbort(reason) so caller can persist partial state when extending deadlines
Keep runtime logic pure; avoid goroutine leaks by guaranteeing all spawned goroutines are tied to a combined cancel and a waitgroup with deterministic teardown
Testing: add deterministic fake stream that can simulate server-side delays, mid-stream disconnects, and delayed writes to validate handoff semantics
Compatibility: API will be additive and opt-in; no breaking changes to existing Stream() function signatures
comments: 2026-02-27 — Lina Gomez: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype adapter that wraps the raw stream and exposes Next(ctx) with a SoftExtend(duration) helper. Prototype lives in local branch: feature/stream-handoff-proto.

2026-03-01 — Aisha Patel: Poked at the prototype with the integration test harness. Found case where SoftExtend after a network jitter still caused the underlying read to return io.EOF; adding a preemptive read buffer mitigates this in most cases. Need to decide whether to expose buffer sizing as option.

2026-03-02 — Review from Ben Wallace: API shape looks good; please add explicit guidance on trace/span propagation when SoftExtend is used. Also request a small benchmark that compares old behavior -> naive context.Cancel_then_retry vs new adapter behavior.
2026-03-04 — Lina Gomez: Pushed changes to prototype, added adjustable prefetch buffer and trace propagation hooks. Opening PR for initial review: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/842

2026-03-05 — QA (Priya Rao): Wrote scenario list for flaky network: (A) mid-message delay, (B) server resets connection, (C) client extends deadline and succeeds. All scenarios reproduced locally. Noted one flaky test that depends on timing; marked as flaky in CI and added retry in harness.

Add a short video demo showing SoftExtend avoiding full prompt retries
